statement: For any positive m,p in characteristic zero, a simple F-rational inverse-Wronski solution W over a monic polynomial with distinct roots s_1,…,s_(mp) in F has local A1-degree ⟨C det B⟩ in the moving-basis affine coordinates, where C=V(s_1,…,s_(mp))(∏_(i=1)^(m−1) i!)^(mp)(−1)^(m(m−1)p/2) and B is the distinguished Plücker-coordinate matrix of Theorem 4.3.

answer.orientation: Moving-basis affine coordinates and ordered distinguished Plücker coordinates in Theorem 4.3

source.location: Section 4, equation (4.2), definition of α(γ,κ), and Theorem 4.3 (printed pp.215–217)
source.version: Published NYJM version, 24 January 2025; corresponding preprint arXiv:2206.01143v1

scope: Simple F-rational W in Gr_F(m,m+p), characteristic zero, with all mp Wronskian roots distinct and F-rational; arbitrary parities.
notes: Choose an ordered basis e_1,…,e_(m+p) with W=span(e_(p+1),…,e_(p+m)). Let F_m(s_l) have rows (e_j(s_l),e_j′(s_l),…,e_j^(m−1)(s_l)). Row (γ,κ), in lexicographic order with 1≤γ≤m and 1≤κ≤p, and column l of B is the minor with row set {κ,p+1,…,p+γ−1,p+γ+1,…,p+m}. V(s) is the source's Vandermonde determinant. This is a local computation with specified coordinates, not a parity-free global invariant; residue-field transfers and non-simple points are deliberately outside this recorded scope. Only the stated sections and proof setup were inspected.
